Introduction:

Rancho Cucamonga Superior Court is a city courthouse situated in San Bernardino and Riverside County California. It is serving the communities of Bloomington, Rancho Cucamonga, Upland, Rialto, Montclair, Chino, Chino Hills, Ontario, Mt. Baldy, Lytle Creek etc. It has jurisdiction over criminal, small claims, civil, family, probate, traffic, and vehicle matters. They also provide online services like online payment, online case search, remote access, court calendar, e-filing etc. so it is not necessary to go to the court for these types of services. Self-help services are provided by every division by appointment only. Proper dressing is required during the court session. Parking facilities are available, one on the east side of the courthouse and one on the southeast side of the courthouse.

How to search for case records?

Rancho Cucamonga Superior Court case search for records can be found online using the court online portal https://cap.sb-court.org/.The court maintains all the records online, in files, or a database. The case search can be done in the following ways:

  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by citation number
  • Searching by party name
  • Searching by business name

After entering data, the case information will be displayed. The portal will only show those records information that is publicly available. The sealed records are not available for the viewing of the public. Some records are unavailable; if the information does not come, the case records will be removed or confidential and cannot be displayed online. You have to go to the court or give a record request for these documents, and then the court will decide whether to provide that information. The fee for each document per page is $0.50, which is mandatory when you come to the court for a records copy.

How do you make payments for tickets?

Rancho Cucamonga Superior Court pay tickets for traffic matters can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the counter service available in the court. Take your ticket and citation number with you when you come for payment. 2% surcharges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

Online

Online payments can be made using the court portal https://cap.sb-court.org/.Retrieve your ticket information by finding your ticket using a case, citation or traffic ticket number. Your case information with the amount of the fine will be displayed. Select the online ticket payment option and pay the amount online. You will receive a confirmation message after your transaction is completed. All fines are not paid online, some cases require a personal appearance and you have to pay at the court. Service charges will be applied in this case.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address; Superior Court of California, County of Bernardino, Attn: Financial Services, BOX 15005, San Bernardino, CA 92415-5005. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number, and account number when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

Phone

Tickets payment can also be made by calling 909-481-4228 or 760-241-9529 24 hours a day. Follow the instructions they tell you. Service charges will be applied in this case.

Drop Box

Ticket payment can be dropped at the drop box in the envelope available at the front door of the court. Please do not put cash in the drop box and write your case and name on the envelope.

How to file a small claim case?

Rancho Cucamonga Superior Court's small claim division handles all cases in which a claim is up to $10000 for individuals and $5000 for companies. You can file a small claim case by filling out the form and submitting it at the clerk's office. Fill in your and the defendant's personal information, and tell the reason for claiming with the number of claims. The notice of appeal sent to the defendant fees is $75. The fees for the case depend upon the amount of money you are suing for. After the form and documents are submitted then the court will send a trial date notice to the defendant. Before the trial date, the defendant or plaintiff can try the mediation facility and try to resolve the matters without appearing in court on the trial date. If the plaintiff fails to appear in court, then the case will be dismissed. After you file the case, start preparing for the trial and research the law, consult an attorney for the information, prepare the evidence, and print all the copies of the evidence for submission. The court commissioner, judge or a temporary judge will hear all the small claims matters.

The family law handles which types of services?

Rancho Cucamonga Superior Court family law division handles family matters that include divorce, separation, domestic violence issues, child custody, support and visitation matters, domestic violence, adoption and elderly abuse cases. The court provides free family facilitators and self-help services to those people that cannot afford an attorney. The facilitators will guide you through the procedure but cannot provide legal advice. Many programs are provided in case of child custody matters that include mediation which can help parents with the difficulty they are facing after the divorce or separation regarding their children.

How can I resolve my traffic tickets?

Rancho Cucamonga Superior Court traffic division handles all traffic and vehicle violation matters. The violation includes accidents, speeding, using a mobile phone during driving, violating traffic signals and traffic rules and many more. You can receive a citation after some days of getting the traffic ticket. If the ticket contains a mandatory appearance, then you have to appear on the schedule. If the court does not contain mandatory appearance, then many options are available that are:

  • Pay the full fine on the time
  • Submit the proof of insurance
  • Enter and send a plea to the court
  • Request for a hearing and appear before the judge
  • Request for a trial by declaration
  • Request for a traffic school

How many pleas can be sent to the court?

Rancho Cucamonga Superior Court plea options are available for some traffic tickets, parking and non-traffic cases. Two types of pleas are available which are:

Plea of guilty

If you are guilty of your actions then write this plea. After sending it the court will review your plea and send you the amount of the fine and there is no need to appear in court.

Plea of not guilty

If you are not guilty of your act, then write this plea. The court will give you a schedule and you have to appear on that day with your proof of innocence.

How many types of juvenile cases are handled by this court?

Rancho Cucamonga Superior Court Juvenile court handles the matters in which a juvenile is involved. Two types of juvenile cases are handled by this court that are:

Juvenile Dependency

It involves cases in which a juvenile is neglected, abused, or in danger and the guardian does not take care of them. This court was concerned with the protection of the child.

Juvenile Delinquency

It involves matters in which the juvenile committed an offense that would be considered criminal if it is done by an adult.

FAQ:

What happens if I do not pay a traffic fine on time?

If you do not pay traffic fines on time then your license will be suspended, extra fines will be added to the previous one and in serious cases, warrants will be issued against you.

What to do if I am unable to pay the fine due to financial hardship?

Send a request with the reason and the salary information to the court if you are unable to pay the fine due to financial hardship.

How can I schedule an appointment online?

You can schedule an appointment for cases through https://bookme.name/RanchoCucamongaDocumentControl. At the date of the appointment, you had to bring your photo ID, payment or waiver form.
